svg.title: An inelastic collision between a disk and a pivoted stick
svg.desc: Top views of a frictionless surface. (a) Before: disk m moves right with velocity v toward the upper tip of a stationary stick M of length r, nailed at its lower end. (b) After: the disk adheres to the tip and the stick and disk rotate clockwise together about the nail with angular velocity ω. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: An inelastic impact conserves angular momentum about the pivot
Fixed pivot: external force, zero torque about pivot
Book values: 0.050 kg disk at 30 m/s; 2.00 kg uniform rod, 1.20 m. Disk treated as a point mass.
Approach playback is slowed more than rotation. L units: kg m²/s; kinetic energy decreases.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
